newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds close weaker in very thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds close weaker in very thin trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed weaker in very thin trade on Tuesday, as the approach of year end prompted many investors to take profits on recent gains, dealers said.

"People have made an awful lot of money in Canada in the last year and they're concerned about leaving a bunch on the table," said one Toronto-based T-bill trader. "They saw the tip of the iceberg of what can happen in Canada last Thursday."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.45 to C$112.10 to yield 6.990 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bonds fell 8/32 to yield 6.48 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds was 51 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Monday.
Canadian bonds saw their biggest one-day drop in more than two years on Thursday as a move by investors to take profits on Canada-U.S. spread narrowing trades prompted panic selling.

"It took a lot of profit off the table for a number of people and they want out. As they get out Canadian domestic accounts are fully invested. It's tough to find new people so we really have to back up prices in order to find buyers," the trader said.
Dealers said a lack of significant Canadian economic news or data was partly responsible for the day's light volumes.
In other prices, the Government of Canada 7.0 percent bond due 2006 fell C$0.28 to C$104.82 to yield 6.340 percent. The U.S. 10-year bond fell 7/32 to yield 6.22 percent.
The spread between the bonds was 12 basis points, unchanged from Monday's closed.
Canada's three-month cash bill traded at 2.93 percent against the U.S. bill at 4.95 percent.
